abstract_summary: RiO-DETR is the first real-time end-to-end transformer for oriented object detection, yet further localization gains require a more expressive box representation. Although distributional regression has succeeded in horizontal DETRs, extending it to oriented detection introduces geometry-misaligned boundary modeling...
citation: RiO-DETRv2: Geometry-Aware Uncertainty Modeling Meets Real-Time Oriented Object Detection Transformer. Zongmin Hu, Zilong He, Yifan Zhao, Xiangyu Yu, Jie Chen, Peixi Wu, Yansong Peng, Hebei Li, Xiaoyan Sun. 2026-10-21. https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29159

AI-TOD-R.AI-TOD-R (Xu et al. 2024) is a large-scale
benchmark for oriented tiny object detection, containing
28,036 images and 752,460 oriented instances across eight
categories. Each image has a resolution of800×800, while
the mean object size is only approximately10.6pixels.
The dataset presents substantial challenges arising from ex-
tremelysmallobjectscales,arbitraryorientations,denseob-
ject arrangements, and imbalanced category distributions.

sultsofDOTAarereturnedbytheofficialserver.Allmodels
are trained on 2 NVIDIA A800 or 4 RTX3090 GPUs. All
latenciesaremeasuredequallyonasingleNVIDIAT4GPU
using TensorRT 10 with FP16 following the same setting of

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard test set evaluation on the official DOTA-1.0 server and standard test sets of DIOR-R and AI-TOD-R, corroborated by latency measurements using TensorRT FP16 on an NVIDIA T4 GPU.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard COCO-style oriented bounding box metrics (mAP50-95, AP50, AP75) computed via official evaluation servers and benchmark protocols against held-out ground truth annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training losses including Varifocal loss, L1 loss, Gaussian KLD loss, fine-grained distribution refinement losses, and auxiliary distillation losses computed against ground-truth labels.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance gains over RiO-DETR and existing detectors align with empirical tables, particularly demonstrating higher accuracy on strict localization thresholds (mAP50-95 and AP75) with negligible computational overhead.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The model is evaluated across three established aerial detection benchmarks (DOTA-1.0 official test server, DIOR-R, and AI-TOD-R) across five model scales, reporting standardized mAP50-95, AP50, AP75, and TensorRT latency measurements against relevant real-time baselines. Component ablations and in-depth analyses of distributional uncertainty and near-square degeneracies validate specific design claims.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard test set evaluation on the official DOTA-1.0 server and standard test sets of DIOR-R and AI-TOD-R, corroborated by latency measurements using TensorRT FP16 on an NVIDIA T4 GPU.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard COCO-style oriented bounding box evaluation metrics (mAP50-95, AP50, AP75) computed via official evaluation servers and benchmark protocols against held-out ground truth annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised loss objectives including Varifocal loss, L1 loss, Gaussian KLD loss, fine-grained distribution refinement losses, and auxiliary distillation losses computed against ground-truth labels.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly analyze precision-recall trade-offs across varying thresholds, the impact of confidence calibration on AP50, and representation ambiguities (canonical-axis exchange) for near-square objects.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, formulating boundary distributions in an object-aligned coordinate frame, handling rotational periodicity through circular-to-local residual refinement, and supervising multi-task branches using Gaussian KLD-derived complete-OBB localization quality alongside distribution-aware confidence calibration.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a sound, well-motivated architectural extension to real-time oriented DETRs with thorough mathematical descriptions, clear ablation studies, and robust benchmarking on standard datasets without methodological circularity.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces RiO-DETRv2, an end-to-end real-time oriented object detection transformer incorporating Object-Aligned Boundary Distribution Refinement, Circular-to-Local Angular Residual Refinement, and Unified OBB Quality-Aligned Learning.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a sound, well-motivated architectural extension to real-time oriented DETRs with thorough mathematical descriptions, clear ablation studies, and robust benchmarking on standard datasets without methodological circularity.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly analyze precision-recall trade-offs across varying thresholds, the impact of confidence calibration on AP50, and representation ambiguities (canonical-axis exchange) for near-square objects.
